newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Taiwan's Int'l Commercial Bank of China.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Taiwan's Int'l Commercial Bank of China.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Wednesday it had assigned Taiwan's International Bank of China an individual rating of B.
At the same time IBCA affirmed the bank's legal rating of 2.

IBCA said in a statement the International Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) established in 1912 as the Bank of China and moved to Taiwan in 1949. In 1971, the bank was partly privatised and changed its name to ICBC.
Almost 43 percent of its shares are indirectly held by the government of the Republic of China, IBCA said.

"ICBC is classified as a private commercial bank in view of its government shareholding being less than 50 percent, affording its greater managerial independence than its majority government-owned peers," the rating agency said. "It does however, maintain strong government links; approximately 15-20 percent of its domestic loan portfolio consists of government related loans."

IBCA said in addition, with its extensive overseas network, the bank benefited from the Central Bank of China, Taiwan's central bank, utilising ICBC's resources to effect U.S. dollar money transfers to distribute funds to diplomatic offices, and for purchase of defence equipment, as well as U.S. dollar clearing.

"By most measures of profitability, capitalisation and liquidity, ICBC is superior to its majority government-owned peers," IBCA said. "This arises from the different management philosophy that drives the bank; whereas the provincial government of Taiwan sets targets for its banks based on volume growth, ICBC's strategy, reflects its greater commercial orientation."

"It has experienced rapid loan growth in recent years, but has managed to maintain good loan book quality. Overdue loans account for 1.8 percent of outstanding loans against a sectoral average close to 4.0 percent," the rating agency said.
